summary.oneLiner: KNR Constructions is transitioning from a low-execution phase to a recovery phase, with HAM projects nearing completion and new EPC orders in Telangana providing near-term revenue visibility; the key catalyst is the resolution of delayed receivables and order inflow from NHAI post-November 2025.

one-line thesis: KNR Constructions is transitioning from a low-execution phase to a recovery phase, with HAM projects nearing completion and new EPC orders in Telangana providing near-term revenue visibility; the key catalyst is the resolution of delayed receivables and order inflow from NHAI post-November 2025.
financial scorecard: Revenue: +12% YoY (H1 FY26: INR1,259cr); EBITDA/margin: 29.8% (consolidated), up from 27.1% H1 FY25; PAT (rptd): INR228cr (H1), +45% YoY; PAT (normalized): INR198cr (ex-INR30cr director variable pay + INR10cr Ramanattukara provision); Order book: INR8,748cr (up from INR7,200cr Mar'25); Net debt: INR2,338cr (consolidated), up from INR1,865cr Mar'25 (net debt/equity 0.49x vs 0.41x); one-offs: INR10cr provision for Ramanattukara viaduct, INR10cr director variable pay, INR30cr total distortions
guidance: Revenue growth: INR2,000cr H2 FY26; Margin: 13-14% EBITDA; Order inflow: INR8,000-10,000cr by FY26 end; Capex/commissioning: INR30-40cr for FY26, mostly for mining development; No new HAM equity infusion beyond INR175cr FY26 and INR117cr FY27
order book & pipeline: INR8,748cr total; Road: 29%; Irrigation: 18%; Mining: 41%; Pipeline: 12%; 81% third-party (76% state, 3% central, 2% private); 19% captive HAM; 1.5-2 year execution horizon excluding mining
segment / subsidiary detail: Road: INR2,537cr order book; Irrigation: INR1,540cr (INR720cr unbilled); Mining: INR3,597cr (Odisha bid INR1,200cr pending); Pipeline: INR1,049cr; Urban flyovers: INR531cr (Hyderabad projects won); HAM: 8 projects, 5 nearing completion (95%+), 2 with delays (Mysore-Kushalnagara P5)
growth verticals / optionality: Entry into solar energy projects via new CEO hire; potential EPC partnerships with IRB and Cube; mining project operational phase (INR300-400cr/year revenue from Year 2); irrigation and state highway expansion in MP, Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu
margins & cost dynamics: EBITDA margin 29.8% consolidated (H1), down from 31.2% H1 FY25 due to INR20cr one-offs (director pay + Ramanattukara provision); core margin remains ~32%; mining margins expected 18-20% in operation phase; irrigation margins pressured by delayed payments
capex / expansion: INR3cr in H1 FY26; full-year guidance INR30-40cr; primarily for mining development (land acquisition, forest clearances, nala diversion); no capex for HAM/EPC as funded by project debt
capital allocation: Priority: debt reduction (net debt/equity 0.49x); HAM equity infusion (INR175cr FY26); mining development capex (INR30-40cr); potential asset monetization of 4 HAM assets (SPA draft circulated, deal expected by Nov 2025 end)
risks & watch-items: Delayed state government payments (INR1,350cr receivables, INR677cr from Kaleshwaram P4); NHAI bidding freeze until Nov 30, 2025; land acquisition delays in mining (Odisha) and highway projects (Mysore-Kushalnagara P5); aggressive bidding in state tenders; potential write-offs if receivables not cleared by Q1FY27
management quality / tone: Cautiously optimistic; acknowledges worst order inflow period in history but confident in NHAI revival post-Nov 2025; proactive on receivables (repeated ministerial meetings); focused on execution, cost control, and diversification into mining/solar
non-obvious takeaways: INR150-200cr of unbilled irrigation revenue expected to be certified in Q3FY26; mining project's INR90cr development phase revenue is non-recurring and will not impact EBITDA margin; asset monetization of 4 HAM assets could reduce net debt by INR500-700cr if closed by Dec 2025
challenges → beneficiaries & losers:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Delayed state government payments | IRB Infra | loser | Medium | Similar exposure to state receivables; KNR's aggressive collection may pressure peers to follow suit, increasing sector-wide liquidity stress |
| NHAI bidding freeze until Nov 30, 2025 | GMR Infrastructure | beneficiary | Low | Larger players may benefit more from NHAI's post-November tender surge due to stronger balance sheets |

themes.title: Infrastructure EPC & roads order-book conversion
themes.need: India's record capital-outlay cycle (roads, metro, marine, hydro, tunnelling) gives diversified EPC contractors multi-year visibility - AFCONS tracks a ~INR4 lakh cr pipeline (70% domestic) and targets ~INR30,000cr FY27 inflow; NCC/DBL/PNCINFRA/GRINFRA/ASHOKA/CEIGALL carry large road/HAM books; AFCONS/PATELENG/AHLUCONT/PSPPROJECT add marine, hydro and building EPC. The binding issue is execution + client-payment cycles, not order intake.
themes.driver: L1-to-firm-order conversion (AFCONS Croatia/Vadhavan, DMRC awards); NHAI/HAM award pickup; monsoon-end execution ramp.

business_model.title: Positioning (investor deck)
business_model.body:
- One of the leading EPC players in Roads & Highways with established presence in Irrigation and Urban Water Infrastructure Management; 30+ years of execution experience, ~9,127 lane km of road projects completed across 12 states.
- Credit ratings reaffirmed by CRISIL: Long Term Bank Facilities at CRISIL AA (Stable) and Short Term ratings at CRISIL A1+ (Stable).
- Founder-promoter-led management — Mr. K. Narasimha Reddy (Managing Director, 50+ years in the Highway sector) and Mr. K. Jalandhar Reddy (Executive Director, 25+ years) — supported by a professional team spanning projects, finance and compliance.
- New vertical entry: Letter of Acceptance from South Eastern Coalfields Limited for coal mining and overburden removal at Kusmunda OCP, Chhattisgarh (JV with Sushee Infra & Mining Limited), marking expansion beyond the traditional roads/irrigation base.
- Strong order book of ₹86,674 Mn as on 30 June 2026, split Roads ₹25,977 Mn, Irrigation & Pipeline ₹25,173 Mn and Mining ₹35,524 Mn.
